words.gloss: one possessing limbs, one having a body

51.meaning: She who is adorned with every kind of ornament.

words.gloss: Kāmeśvara, Śiva as the Divine Consort

52.meaning: She who is seated on the lap of Śiva-Kāmeśvara.

words.gloss: the Auspicious One; feminine form of Śiva

53.meaning: The Auspicious Goddess, the Divine Power of Śiva.

words.gloss: devoted to, under the influence of

54.meaning: She whose beloved Lord is completely devoted to her.

words.gloss: Mount Meru, the golden axial mountain (सु = excellent, golden + मेरु = Meru)

55.meaning: She who dwells on the central peak of Mount Meru.
55.note: Of Meru's three summits, the middle one bears Her city.

words.gloss: possessing श्री — splendour, auspiciousness, prosperity (श्री + मतुप्; nominative श्रीमान्, stem श्रीमत् in composition)
city — here Śrīnagara / Śrīpura, the city on Meru's middle peak, where the previous nama has just placed us
mistress, sovereign lady, leader (feminine of नायक, from नी "to lead": नी + ण्वुल् → नायक)

56.meaning: The Sovereign Lady of the resplendent City.
56.note:
Sandhi: श्रीमत् + नगर → श्रीमन्नगर। The final त् before the nasal न् assimilates in nasality (Pāṇini 8.4.45, यरोऽनुनासिकेऽनुनासिको वा), giving न् + न → न्न। The visible न्न is thus a joint, not a doubled root consonant.

Two readings are current. Descriptive: श्रीमत् qualifies नगर — the city possesses श्री, and She rules it. Proper name: श्रीमन्नगर taken as the city's own name (Śrīmannagara = Śrīnagara / Śrīpura), hence "the Lady of Śrīnagara"; Bhāskararāya reads the compound this way.

Namas 55–58 form a nested descent inward — Meru's middle peak (55) → the city upon it (56) → the cintāmaṇi palace within the city (57) → the pañcabrahma seat within the palace (58). This nama is the second ring. The root नी here also anticipates Her sovereign and commander namas in the Bhaṇḍāsura war section.

57.meaning: She who abides within the palace built of wish-fulfilling gems.
57.note: The Cintāmaṇi-gṛha stands at the heart of Śrīnagara.

words.gloss: the Brahmas — Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, Sadāśiva

58.meaning: She who is seated on the couch formed of the five Brahmās.
58.note: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra and Īśvara form its four legs; Sadāśiva is the plank (फलक) on which She rests.

59.meaning: She who abides in the vast forest of great lotuses.
59.note: The compound splits at पद्म + अटवी (a → ā), so the surface महापद्माटवी hides a four-member sequence rather than three. And संस्था here carries the सम् prefix, a slight intensification over the plain स्था used in the previous verse's namas.

60.meaning: She who dwells in the grove of kadamba trees.

61.meaning: She who abides in the midst of the ocean of nectar.

62.meaning: She whose eyes are filled with love.
62.note: Or, taking काम as the object given: "whose glance grants what is desired."

63.meaning: She who bestows all that is desired.

words.gloss: seers, sages (देव + ऋषि → देवर्षि, अ + ऋ → अर्)
being praised, being hymned (passive participle of स्तु "to praise")

64.meaning: She whose own glory is hymned by the massed hosts of gods and sages.

words.gloss: girded up, ready, intent upon (उत् + युक्त; वध + उद्युक्त → वधोद्युक्त)
accompanied by, attended by (सम् + अनु + इता)

65.meaning: She who is attended by the army of Śaktis girded for the slaying of Bhaṇḍāsura.

words.gloss: wealth, abundance (सम्पत्) + maker, fem. (करी) → Sampatkarī, commander of Her elephant division
mounted upon (सम् + आ + रूढ, from रुह्)

66.meaning: She who is attended by the elephant host led by Sampatkarī, seated upon it.

words.gloss: horse (अश्व) + mounted (आरूढा) → Aśvārūḍhā, commander of Her cavalry
a crore → कोटिकोटिभिः = by crores upon crores (instrumental plural)

67.meaning: She who is encompassed by crores upon crores of steeds marshalled by Aśvārūḍhā.
67.note:
Nama 66 pairs with 65: the Śakti army named there is now itemised by division — elephants under Sampatkarī, cavalry under Aśvārūḍhā.

Text: the Devanagari reads कोटिकोटिभिरावृता (ट, not ठ). The सिंधुर / सिन्धुर difference is only anusvāra versus conjunct spelling; both are current, and the verse line keeps the anusvāra form.

words.gloss: king, chief → चक्रराज = Cakrarāja, the sovereign cakra, here the name of Her own nine-tiered chariot
mounted upon, having ascended (आ + रूढ, from रुह्)
fully equipped, furnished, decked out (परि + कृता, with ष् by the ruki rule)

68.meaning: She who, mounted upon the chariot Cakrarāja, is fully equipped with every weapon.

words.gloss: that which is to be sung, song, music (from गै "to sing")
wheel, cakra → गेयचक्र = Geyacakra, the "chariot of song"
the Minister — Śyāmalā (Rāja-mātaṅgī), Her prime minister (feminine of मन्त्रिन्)
closely attended upon, waited on all round (परि + सेविता)

69.meaning: She who is closely attended by the Minister Śyāmalā, mounted upon the Geyacakra chariot.
69.note: These two open the chariot sequence — 68 is the Goddess's own Cakrarāja, 69 the Geyacakra of Her minister Śyāmalā, and 70 follows with the Kiricakra of Daṇḍanāthā (Vārāhī).

words.gloss: boar, hog → किरिचक्र = Kiricakra, the "boar chariot" of Vārāhī
mistress, lady → दण्डनाथा = Daṇḍanāthā (Vārāhī), commander-in-chief, wielder of the rod of punishment
placed in front, led by, honoured (पुरः + कृता)

70.meaning: She who is preceded by Daṇḍanāthā, mounted upon the Kiricakra chariot.

words.gloss: the garlanded one (मालिनी + क) → ज्वालामालिनिका = Jvālāmālinī, the Śakti garlanded with flames
flung up, cast out, projected (आ + क्षिप्त, from क्षिप् "to throw")
middle, centre (मध्य) + abiding in, situated in (गा, from गम्) → she who dwells at the centre

71.meaning: She who abides at the centre of the rampart of fire flung up by Jvālāmālinī.
71.note: Nama 70 closes the chariot triad (Cakrarāja, Geyacakra, Kiricakra); 71 turns to the fiery rampart Jvālāmālinī threw up around the host in the war against Bhaṇḍāsura.

words.gloss: girded up, ready, intent upon (उत् + युक्त; वध + उद्युक्त → वधोद्युक्त)

72.meaning: She who is delighted by the valour of the Śaktis girded for the slaughter of Bhaṇḍa's army.

words.gloss: the Nityās, the fifteen eternal Śaktis of the lunar days
keenly eager, full of longing (सम् + उत्सुका)

73.meaning: She who is eager to behold the swelling valour of the Nityā deities.
73.note: Nama 72 answers 65 — there She is attended by the Śaktis girded to slay Bhaṇḍāsura himself, here gladdened by their prowess against his army. In 72–73 the Goddess is watcher rather than combatant: delighted, then eager to watch on.

words.gloss: son → भण्डपुत्र = the sons of Bhaṇḍāsura (thirty, per the Lalitopākhyāna)
girded up, intent upon (उत् + युक्त; वध + उद्युक्त → वधोद्युक्त)
Bālā, the young Goddess Bālā Tripurasundarī, Her nine-year-old daughter

74.meaning: She who is gladdened by the valour of Bālā, girded to slay the sons of Bhaṇḍāsura.

words.gloss: mother, revered lady → मन्त्रिण्यम्बा = Mother Mantriṇī (मन्त्रिणी + अम्बा → मन्त्रिण्यम्बा, ई + अ → य् अ)
pleased, gratified, satisfied (from तुष् "to be content")

75.meaning: She who is gratified by the slaying of Viṣaṅga wrought by Mother Mantriṇī.
75.note: Namas 74–75 continue the spectator sequence, now naming who kills whom — Bālā takes Bhaṇḍāsura's sons, Mantriṇī takes his brother Viṣaṅga, and 76 gives Vārāhī the other brother, Viśukra.

words.gloss: taking away, carrying off (from हृ "to seize")
Vārāhī, i.e. Daṇḍanāthā, the boar-faced commander-in-chief

76.meaning: She who is gladdened by the might of Vārāhī in taking the life of Viśukra.

words.gloss: a look, glance, beholding (आ + लोक; मुख + आलोक → मुखालोक)
Lord of the gaṇas, Gaṇeśa → गणेश्वरा, feminine bahuvrīhi: "she by whom he was made"

77.meaning: She who brought forth Śrī Gaṇeśvara by a glance at the face of Kāmeśvara.
77.note: Nama 76 closes the roll of slain commanders — Bhaṇḍāsura's sons to Bālā, Viṣaṅga to Mantriṇī, Viśukra to Vārāhī. 77 turns to Viśukra's Jayavighna yantra, which had struck the host with torpor: at Her glance upon Kāmeśvara's face Gaṇeśa arose and broke the obstruction.

words.gloss: Gaṇeśa → महागणेश = Mahāgaṇeśa, the great Gaṇeśa born of Her glance
shattered, split apart, broken through (निः + भिन्न, from भिद् "to cleave")
yantra, mystic device → विघ्नयन्त्र = the Jayavighna yantra of obstruction
greatly delighted, thrilled (प्र + हर्षिता, intensive of हृष्)

78.meaning: She who was thrilled when Mahāgaṇeśa shattered the yantra of obstruction.

words.gloss: chief, foremost, lord → भण्डासुरेन्द्र = Bhaṇḍāsura, lord of the asuras
she who rains down, showers forth (from वृष् "to rain")

79.meaning: She who rains down counter-missiles against the weapons discharged by Bhaṇḍāsura, lord of demons.
79.note: शस्त्र and अस्त्र are not interchangeable — शस्त्र is the ordinary weapon, अस्त्र the missile impelled by mantra, so प्रत्यस्त्र is the mantra-answer to what he throws. 79 is also where the Goddess stops watching and enters the fight Herself.

words.gloss: form → दशाकृतिः = the ten forms, the ten avatāras

80.meaning: She from whose fingernails sprang forth the ten forms of Nārāyaṇa.
80.note:
Text: the ङ्गु ligature in कराङ्गुलि had dropped its ङ् in the scanned Devanagari, a common loss.

Nama 80 ends in a visarga (दशाकृतिः, an -i stem nominative), unlike the -ā endings around it — worth keeping when reciting the pair.

words.gloss: of Paśupati (Śiva) → महापाशुपतास्त्र, Śiva's supreme missile
soldier (सैनिक) → सैनिका, feminine to agree with Her

81.meaning: She by whom the demon soldiery was burnt to ash in the fire of the great Pāśupata missile.
81.note: Nama 81 chains three a + a → ā joins in a row (पाशुपत + अस्त्र, अस्त्र + अग्नि, निर्दग्ध + असुर), which is why the surface form hides so many members.

words.gloss: Kāmeśvara, Her consort → कामेश्वरास्त्र = the Kāmeśvara missile
burnt down utterly, reduced to ash (निः + दग्ध, from दह्)
together with, along with (the prefix स in the sense of सह)
Śūnyaka, Bhaṇḍāsura's capital city (शून्य = empty, void) → शून्यका, feminine bahuvrīhi agreeing with Her

82.meaning: She by whom Śūnyaka, along with Bhaṇḍāsura himself, was burnt to ash by the Kāmeśvara missile.
vigraha: कामेश्वरास्त्रेण निर्दग्धं सभण्डासुरं शून्यकं यया सा।

words.gloss: Brahmā (ब्रह्म in compound; ब्रह्म + उपेन्द्र → ब्रह्मोपेन्द्र)
fully extolled, praised in chorus (सम् + स्तुत, from स्तु)
glory, majesty, greatness (वैभव) → वैभवा, feminine bahuvrīhi

83.meaning: She whose glory is extolled by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra and the other gods.
vigraha: ब्रह्मोपेन्द्रमहेन्द्रादिभिः देवैः संस्तुतं वैभवं यस्याः सा।
83.note: Nama 82 ends the war — the city Śūnyaka burns with its lord. 83 answers 64: there Her glory was hymned by the massed hosts of gods and sages, here by the chief gods named one by one, with the victory now behind it.

words.gloss: fire → नेत्राग्नि = the fire of that eye
wholly burnt, consumed (सम् + दग्ध, from दह् "to burn")
Kāma, Manmatha, the god of love
healing herb, medicament (संजीवन + औषधि → संजीवनौषधि, अ + औ → औ)

84.meaning: She who is the life-restoring herb for Kāma, burnt to ash by the fire of Hara's eye.

words.gloss: glorious, resplendent (श्रीमत् + वाग्भव → श्रीमद्वाग्भव, त् → द् before voiced व)
the Vāgbhava kūṭa, first segment of the Pañcadaśī mantra (वाक् = speech + भव = origin, "the source of speech")
peak, segment, cluster — a kūṭa of the mantra
one, sole, single (कूट + एक → कूटैक, अ + ए → ऐ)
lotus (पङ्क = mud + ज = born) → मुखपङ्कजा = she whose face is a lotus

85.meaning: She whose lotus face is one in essence with the glorious Vāgbhava kūṭa.
85.note: Nama 84 pivots from war to grace — the Kāma burnt in the old myth is revived by Her. 85 opens the mantra-body sequence: the three kūṭas of the Pañcadaśī are mapped onto Her form, Vāgbhava as the face here, Kāmarāja from neck to waist in 86, and the Śakti kūṭa below the waist in 87.

words.gloss: extending as far as, up to (परि + अन्त)
segment of the mantra → मध्यकूट = the middle kūṭa, i.e. the Kāmarāja kūṭa
she who has that as her very form (स्वरूप + इनी)

86.meaning: She whose form from below the throat down to the waist is the middle, Kāmarāja, kūṭa.

words.gloss: Śakti, power → शक्तिकूट = the third segment of the Pañcadaśī
oneness, identity (एक + ता; कूट + एकता → कूटैकता, अ + ए → ऐ)
attained, come into, arrived at (आ + पन्न; एकता + आपन्न → एकतापन्न)
below (कटि + अधः → कट्यधः, इ + अ → य्)
she who bears, carries (from धृ "to bear")

87.meaning: She who bears the portion below the waist as having become one with the Śakti kūṭa.
87.note: Namas 85–87 close the triad — Vāgbhava as the face, Kāmarāja from throat to waist, Śakti kūṭa below it. The three namas together say that the Pañcadaśī mantra and Her body are one thing, so that reciting the mantra is itself the worship of Her form.

words.gloss: mantra → मूलमन्त्र = the root mantra, the Pañcadaśī (or Ṣoḍaśī)
whose self or essence it is (from आत्मन्, feminine)

88.meaning: She whose very self is the root mantra.

words.gloss: root → मूलकूट = the kūṭas of the root mantra
body, bodily frame (कलेबर, variant of कलेवर) → कलेबरा, feminine

89.meaning: She whose body is the three kūṭas of the root mantra.

words.gloss: the Kula, the Kaula lineage and its inner meaning
one, sole, alone (अमृत + एक → अमृतैक, अ + ए → ऐ)
she who savours, relishes, has a taste for (from रस "flavour, relish")

90.meaning: She who delights in the nectar of Kula alone.

words.gloss: secret sign, esoteric convention, agreed code (सम् + केत)

91.meaning: She who guards the secret conventions of the Kula tradition.
91.note:
Namas 88–89 carry the mantra-body identity of 85–87 to its conclusion — first the mantra as Her self, then its three kūṭas as Her frame. 90–91 then turn to the Kaula transmission that guards it.

Text: कलेबर and कलेवर are both attested; the ब / व interchange is normal, and LSN editions usually print कलेबरा.

words.gloss: family, noble lineage; in Śrīvidyā, the Kula — Śakti, the mūlādhāra
woman, lady, one of graceful limbs (from अङ्ग "limb")

92.meaning: The Lady of the Kula — she who is the woman of that noble house.

words.gloss: the Kula (also read as the mūlādhāra, or the assembly of tattvas)

93.meaning: She who abides within the Kula.

words.gloss: belonging to the Kula, of the Kaula path — vṛddhi derivative of कुल
the presiding Goddess of Kaula worship; the Śakti in the mūlādhāra who joins kula (Śakti) to akula (Śiva)

94.meaning: She who is the Deity of the Kaula path.

words.gloss: yoginī, female adept; she who is joined, who unites (from युज् "to yoke")
kula (कुल) → अकुल = that which is past kula; in Kaula usage Akula is Śiva, seated in the sahasrāra, as Kula is Śakti

96.meaning: She who is Akula — beyond the Kula, one with Śiva.

words.gloss: the Samaya doctrine and its worship; literally agreement, convention — also read as सम + अय, the state in which Śiva and Śakti are equal

97.meaning: She who abides within the Samaya path.

words.gloss: intent upon, holding that as highest (तत् + पर) → तत्परा, feminine

98.meaning: She who is devoted to the observances of the Samaya path.
98.note:
Namas 92–96 belong to the Kaula reckoning and 97–98 to the Samaya, the two being the outer and the inner worship — Samaya performed within the six cakras and held the higher by Bhāskararāya. The sequence honours both, and 96 अकुला is the hinge: having been named through Kula five times, She is then named as what lies past it.

अन्तस्था in 93 and 97 is अन्तः + स्था with the visarga assimilated, as in 57 चिन्तामणिगृहान्तस्था.

words.gloss: support, base, foundation → मूलाधार = the root-support cakra at the base of the spine
one, sole, alone (आधार + एक → आधारैक, अ + ए → ऐ)
abode, dwelling; she whose abode it is (नि + लय)

99.meaning: She whose sole abode is the mūlādhāra.

words.gloss: Brahmā → ब्रह्मग्रन्थि = the Brahma-knot, first of the three obstructing knots, at the mūlādhāra
she who splits open, pierces, sunders (वि + भेदिनी, from भिद् "to cleave")
filled, replete; also city → मणिपूर = the navel cakra, "the one filled with gems"
within, inside (मणिपूर + अन्तः → मणिपूरान्तः; अन्तः + उदिता → अन्तरुदिता, visarga → र् before a vowel)
risen, arisen, come forth (उत् + इता, from इ "to go")

101.meaning: She who rises up within the Maṇipūra cakra.

words.gloss: Viṣṇu → विष्णुग्रन्थि = the Viṣṇu-knot, second of the three, at the heart (anāhata)
she who pierces, splits open (वि + भिद्)

102.note: From 99 the namas trace the kuṇḍalinī ascent, and they alternate — a cakra reached, then the knot above it broken. The three granthis are Brahma at the base, Viṣṇu at the heart, Rudra at the brow; 103–104 complete the pattern with आज्ञाचक्रान्तरालस्था and रुद्रग्रन्थिविभेदिनी before the sahasrāra is reached in 105.

words.gloss: command → आज्ञाचक्र, the wheel of command at the brow

103.meaning: She who abides in the interior of the Ājñā cakra.

words.gloss: Rudra → रुद्रग्रन्थि, the last knot, at the brow
thousand (सहस्र) + spoke (अर) → सहस्रार, the thousand-petalled crown cakra

105.meaning: She who has ascended the thousand-petalled lotus.

words.gloss: she who showers down abundantly (अभि + वृष्)

106.meaning: She who showers down the very essence of nectar.
106.note: The ascent completes at 105 and then reverses direction: 106 pours the amṛta back down. The root वृष् recurs from nama 79 — counter-missiles rained on Bhaṇḍāsura there, nectar on the devotee here. Likewise आरूढा, last seen mounting war-chariots in 67–70, now mounts a lotus.
